feedback: Penny's confession follows the available physical chain and her already admitted opportunities. Opening during preview and poisoning the waiting glass confirm an inferred sequence rather than introduce a missing mechanism or secret access. The price-collar cover, repayment that could not erase betrayal, and fear of family reaction were all available before voting. Her final inability to manage their response gives the confession emotional consequence. Hugh and Barb own their separate wrongdoing, which makes the ending more credible than blanket innocence. Hugh's speech does not resolve his earlier press-version claim, so that ambiguity persists, but it does not supply a new decisive fact needed to identify Penny. The outcome feels earned despite the evidence supporting inference rather than exclusive forensic proof.
